correctness.rationale: The unique greedy decomposition is proved to equal the exact subsequence-universality index. Transition counts are j-1 known and q-j new letters within each arch, with q versus q-1 initial choices. Multiplication by the incomplete-tail functions gives the complete joint generating function. The uniformly chosen proper infinite word yields i.i.d. cover-time blocks L=1+sum_{j=1}^{q-1}Geom((q-j)/(q-1)); exact mean/variance and the renewal CLT give the stated rates. Independent exhaustive coefficient enumeration for q=2 through n=10, q=3 through n=12, q=4 through n=9, and q=5 through n=7 agrees with direct index computation, and direct scattered-subsequence tests corroborate short cases. The q=2 zero-variance boundary is separately stated. No finite enumeration substitutes for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural homogeneous adjacency constraint on q-ary words changes the entire universality-index distribution. The theorem gives a closed rational bivariate series uniform in both q and the index, rather than per-length numerical computations; its renewal identification removes post-arch dependence and yields explicit growth and fluctuation constants for every q>=3, with a sharp deterministic boundary at q=2. The exact distribution and CLT are relevant to universality under proper-coloring/transition-constrained string sources, and are not merely a renaming or a single small instance of a known table.
